Orientation Camp for Undergraduate 2025 Batch Concluded
Thursday, 08 January 2026
1692 Hits
The Orientation Camp for the 100 newly admitted students of the 2025 batch of medical students was conducted in the Gandhi Ashram, Sevagram. The 2-week residential camp, which commenced on 25 December 2025, is part of a foundation course at MGIMS, Sevagram for the medical students and is designed to orient students to a value system based on Gandhian ideology and assist them in adapting to the institute's environment.
Imminent Gandhians and thought leaders from diverse fields across the country were invited to interact with the students. The names included Shri Barun Mitra, Prof Jeevan Kumar, Dr Satish Gogulwar, Prof John Chelladurai, Dr Avinash Saoji, Dr Ulhas Jajoo, Dr. Sunil Ganatra, Shri Atul Sharma, Shri Vijay Tambe, Dr Siby Joseph.  The objective behind introduction to the Gandhian ideology and Sarvodaya vichar is to bring an attitudinal change among students towards rural development, service to downtrodden, reaching the unreached & community participation in health activities.
Other activities included skill-building workshops such as 'Values in Health Care: A Spiritual Approach' (VIHASA), and sessions on 'Key to Health', 'Personal & Professional Development', 'Emotional well-being and Healthy choices', and 'Humanities in Health'. The daily routine includes all-religion prayers, yoga, and meditation to foster spiritual health. To instil the dignity of labour, students actively engaged in Shramdaan activities, cleaning the premises, helping in the kitchen work, and spinning yarn on the Charkha.  Visits to historical places like Bapu Kuti, Pavnar Ashram, and Gitai Mandir were also integrated into the program to instil social consciousness in the aspiring physicians.
The camp concluded with a valedictory function where Shri Gautam Bhai Bajaj from Pavnar Ashram graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. He guided the students regarding the importance of care, love, and empathy while providing healthcare services. Shri PL Tapdiya, President, Kasturba Health Society, reiterated the objectives of the camp and emphasized to the students that it is important to become a good citizen first before becoming a doctor.
